claims: NASA’s Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
Artemis II sends four astronauts on a 10-day around-the-Moon journey.
Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II tests the SLS rocket.
Artemis II includes astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew is currently in orbit following a successful launch on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II is scheduled for approximately 10 days.
The objective of Artemis II is to validate the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft for future lunar landings.
Reid Wiseman is the Commander of Artemis II.
Victor Glover is the Pilot of Artemis II.
Christina Koch is the Mission Specialist of Artemis II.
Jeremy Hansen is a Canadian Space Agency astronaut on Artemis II.
The Artemis II crew will travel farther from Earth than anyone has ever been.
The Artemis II crew will surpass the record set by Apollo 13 in 1970.
Artemis II launched from Kennedy Space Center, Florida (Pad 39B).
The Artemis II mission involves a complex deep-space trajectory intended to test navigation and environmental systems.
The Artemis II mission culminates with a high-speed 2,700°C re-entry testing the heat shield for future missions.
The Artemis II crew is scheduled to fly around the Moon and return.
